verdicts.title: Python 3.12 is claimed by eleven pyproject classifiers with zero CI coverage and no documented endpoints-only policy
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual link verified in the current tree. `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` returns nothing (exit 1) across all workflows, composite actions and scripts; the only python-version values anywhere in .github are "3.11" and "3.13" (build-distributions.yml:37,129; ci.yml:56,69,117,131; pr.yml:96,109,165,182; prepare-release-implementation.yml:335,353,421,440; validate-distributions.yml:19 matrix ["3.11","3.13"]; python-tests.yml:34-38 input defaults to "3.11"). Meanwhile `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` in the root plus all ten packages/*/pyproject.toml, and 'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12' appears in all eleven pyprojects (root:29, accounting:23, alignment:26, auditing:21, base:21, dpftrl:21, dpsgd:21, engine:21, optimizers:21, patches:21, transformers:28). No endpoints-only policy is written down: CONTRIBUTING.md:162-166 says only 'minimum (Python 3.11) and latest (Python 3.13) dependency validation' and AGENTS.md's lane list names only 3.11/3.13; a grep for any 'supported endpoints' statement finds nothing outside unrelated accounting-calibration prose. GitHub confirms issue #841 is closed with state_reason 'not_planned' and zero comments, and its parent #774 is still OPEN, so the acceptance criteria were declined silently rather than satisfied. Caveats that keep this at low: the gap is metadata/process only, no privacy guarantee or numeric result is involved, 3.11 and 3.13 bracket the interpreter range, and the maintainer (repo owner) explicitly closed the tracking issue as not_planned - so this is a re-raise of a recorded wontfix, valuable mainly because the decision was never documented.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: All eleven distributions publish the 'Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12' classifier with requires-python '>=3.11,<3.14', while no CI lane in the repository ever runs any Python 3.12 interpreter (zero '3.12' occurrences anywhere under .github/). A 3.12-only resolver or interpreter regression would therefore reach a published wheel whose metadata advertises 3.12 with no CI signal having existed. No privacy guarantee, epsilon value, or numeric result is affected. Secondary cost: neither AGENTS.md nor CONTRIBUTING.md records an endpoints-only testing policy, and issue #841 was closed not_planned without a comment, so a future reader cannot distinguish a deliberate choice from the drift introduced when the 3.12 lanes were retargeted to 3.13.

verdicts.title: CONTRIBUTING.md routes contributors to GitHub Discussions, which is disabled on the public repository
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. CONTRIBUTING.md:87 ('- [Open Discussions](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)' under 'Finding Issues to Work On') and CONTRIBUTING.md:445 ('- **Questions**: Open a [Discussion](...)' under '## Getting Help') both still route contributors to Discussions. api.github.com/repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque reports visibility 'public', private false, has_issues true, has_discussions FALSE; an anonymous GET of /discussions returns 403 while /issues returns 200 from the same client. GitHub confirms #566 is closed state_reason 'not_planned', and the closing comment is explicit that this was intentional: 'Withdrawing GitHub Discussions from the public-source preparation scope for now. The repository can remain focused on Issues and the private security-reporting channel.' That comment makes the two surviving links definitively stale rather than forward-looking. No link checker exists in CI (no lychee / linkcheck / markdown-link-check anywhere in .github/ or mkdocs.yml), so nothing catches it. Only remaining ambiguity: whether GitHub would serve 404 rather than 403 to a non-proxied client - immaterial, since has_discussions=false is authoritative and either code is a dead end for the reader. Severity stays low: contributor-doc dead link, no code, no privacy impact.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: An external contributor reading CONTRIBUTING.md follows either of the two Discussions links (lines 87 and 445) and reaches a dead page - the repository is public with has_discussions=false, and an anonymous request to /discussions returns 403 while /issues returns 200. The maintainer's own closing comment on #566 states the repo will stay on Issues plus private security reporting, so the routing contradicts the recorded decision. Impact is limited to contributor-onboarding friction and questions landing in the wrong place; nothing executable, no privacy or numeric consequence.

verdicts.title: docs/reference/rng.md calls optimizer.step(), which the functional optimizer does not have
verdicts.reasoning: Verified in the current tree and by execution. docs/reference/rng.md:325 is `optimizer.step(noisy_grads)`, inside the determinism example at :306-326; `grep -rn 'optimizer\.step' docs/ examples/ README.md` returns exactly that one hit. Ran `uv run python -c 'from opaque.optimizers import sgd; o = sgd(lr=0.01)'`: type is torchopt.base.GradientTransformation, public members are exactly ['chain','count','index','init','update'], hasattr(o,'step') is False - so the documented call raises AttributeError. Every other end-to-end snippet uses the correct idiom (docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:150-151 and examples/quickstart.py:88-89 both do `updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(...)` then `torchopt.apply_updates(params, updates)`). `git show 12146ec4 -- docs/reference/rng.md` confirms that commit rewrote line 322 of the same block (`gaussian_noise(1.1, ...)` -> keyword form) and left :325 untouched, so the hand-edit-without-execution mechanism is real. Two honest discounts: the block is a sketch with several undefined names (`model`, `batch`, `optimizer`, and `compute_dp_grads`, which exists nowhere in docs/, examples/ or packages/), so a reader cannot paste it verbatim in any case; and the error is loud, not silent. Low severity: docs only, no privacy or numerical consequence. Note the open documentation umbrella #775 ('Reconcile documentation and citations with post-remediation code') is generic and its only open child #845 is about citations, so I did not mark this as already tracked.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/reference/rng.md:325 tells the reader to call `optimizer.step(noisy_grads)`, but `opaque.optimizers.sgd(...)` returns a torchopt GradientTransformation with no `step` member (verified: members are chain/count/index/init/update), so the documented idiom raises AttributeError and contradicts the correct `optimizer.update(...)` + `torchopt.apply_updates(...)` pair used in docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:150-151 and examples/quickstart.py:88-89. The surrounding block is a pseudo-code sketch (undefined `model`, `batch`, `optimizer`, and a `compute_dp_grads` helper that exists nowhere in the repository), so the practical cost is a misleading API idiom in the RNG reference rather than a copy-pasteable crash. Docs-only; no privacy or numerical effect.

verdicts.title: Sweep B's structural criterion is unmet: no generator or CI check ties published defaults and accepted-value lists to their dataclasses
verdicts.reasoning: The structural claim holds, with two evidence corrections. Verified: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:148-155 is a hand-written mechanism/sampler/default-kwargs table and :157-165 the prose accepted-value list; the sources of truth are _SAMPLER_BY_MECHANISM (_training_arguments.py:186-195), _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS (:204-212), _CLIPPING_KWARGS/_SAMPLING_KWARGS/_MECHANISM_KWARGS (:214-238), _NOISE_CALIBRATION_KWARGS (:240) and _MECH_DEFAULTS (:254-262). No generator and no check exists: only two files under packages/*/tests and tests/ mention 'docs/' (opaque-patches/tests/torch/test_cpu_offload.py and tests/integration/alignment/test_mechanism_agnostic.py) and both are prose comments; nothing imports the dicts and parses the Markdown; no script in scripts/ or step in .github/ reads a docs file; mkdocs.yml has no generator (mkdocstrings + pymdownx.snippets only, neither wired to these tables). I re-checked the tables line by line and they do match the code today (including the subtlety that 'bound' appears in _MECHANISM_KWARGS['gaussian'] only to raise a targeted ConfigurationError at :1222, so its absence from the docs is correct - which incidentally shows a naive generated check would need care). Corrections to the finding: (a) the evidence's symbol names _MECHANISM_SAMPLERS / _ALLOWED_SAMPLING_MODES / _MECHANISM_DEFAULT_KWARGS do not exist - the real names are the ones above; (b) the evidence's claim that ba39783d (PR #1026) was 'a documentation-only edit; no generator, no test' is wrong: that commit also changed _dp_trainer.py and _training_arguments.py and added TestPrivacyDefaults::test_unset_privacy_delta_uses_dataset_dependent_default to packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_dp_trainer.py, which pins the 1/n**1.1 delta default behaviourally. So the epsilon-affecting half of the family did get a behaviour test; what remains unguarded is only the docs-vs-dataclass table sync. Because the tables are correct today, this is a missing-regression-guard finding with no current user-visible defect, which is why it stays low. Also note docs/reference/transformers.md:185-199 is a second hand-maintained copy of the same defaults.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: There is no generator or CI check tying docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:148-165 (and the second copy in docs/reference/transformers.md:185-199) to _SAMPLER_BY_MECHANISM, _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS, _MECHANISM_KWARGS and _MECH_DEFAULTS in packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py: no test reads any docs file, no script or CI step does, and mkdocs build --strict does not read Python. The tables and accepted-value lists are accurate at this commit, so no user is misled today; the exposure is that the next edit to a mechanism's default kwargs or sampler allow-list can silently desynchronize the published table again, as it did three times before. PR #1026 did add one behaviour test pinning the 1/n**1.1 default delta, so the epsilon-relevant default is guarded; the unguarded part is documentation accuracy only.
